messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.reasoning:
We need to call function user_mandates twice: once for parath, once for bhanu. The user wants all pending and active mandates. The function signature allows status optional; but we can pass status? It expects one status. We cannot request both statuses at once. So we need to call twice? Actually we can call with status "active" and then "pending". But the user wants all pending and active mandates. We could call with status unspecified? That defaults to active. So we need two calls: one for active, one for pending. But the user says "all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu". So we need to fetch both statuses for each user. We can call user_mandates twice per user. Or we can call partner_mandates? No, partner_mandates fetches mandates for partner, not user. So we need user_mandates.

Thus we need to call user_mandates twice for each user. But we might combine? The function only accepts one status. So we need separate calls. We can do:

Call user_mandates({"name":"parath","status":"active"}) and user_mandates({"name":"parath","status":"pending"}). Similarly for bhanu.
